articles.detail: 5 cycles, all completed; avg 12 published per cycle; 0 quarantined

experiment: Skipped. Every target is met, no experiment is active, and the pause gate (`noNewExperimentsUntil` 2026-11-05) bars a new one; nothing was evaluated or changed.
weakestArea: Science is the thinnest margin: 6 against 5, down from 10 yesterday. Two cycles (05:00, 14:00) went under the per-cycle floor at 1 because the feed carried no Nature, Science, Quanta, New Scientist, STAT or Carbon Brief findings, and the selector rightly skipped author-list-only paper stubs rather than pad. This is the allowed shortfall; the lever is more science sources, not a higher floor.
watching: Gulf war: Iran escalated Hormuz strikes, a second tanker fire was reported off Bandar Abbas, the US is drafting its biggest bomb strike on Iran and wants a bigger IEA oil release.
Food security: the UN set a weeks-long fertilizer deadline over Hormuz, Egypt released wheat for bread, and Afghan hunger hit a record.
Yemen: the Houthis struck the Aden palace and Taiz is encircled with prices tripled.
Brazil: Bolsonaro edges Lula in polling, Meta throttled a Brazilian campaign, and Brazil ended the six-day work week.
AI industry: Anthropic's revenue rose 45% while its valuation faces a markdown, and a US regulator opened a probe of OpenAI and Anthropic.
North Korea: a submarine fired missiles as China and North Korea opened the Dandong bridge.
Pakistan: Peshawar security emergency, a school roof collapse, and Bannu ending Afghan doctors' training.
EU: leaders failed to agree the 2028-2034 budget.
coverageGaps: Oceania had no datelines for a second day running.
Science fell to 6 from 10; two cycles found no peer-reviewed findings in the feed beyond Phys.org and New Scientist.
Europe had 8 datelines, down from 14 yesterday.
Three stories rest only on state or advocacy sources (Colombia's Jerusalem embassy, the EU budget, the UN Hormuz fertilizer warning), down from five.
context: Multi-source rose to 38% (24 of 63) from 25%, the first day above target this week, and Al Jazeera's share fell to 14% from 19%. US datelines held at 22% and Latin America at 6% (Brasília, Rio de Janeiro, two Brazil stories). Cycles averaged 1031s with all five completing.
